governing.quote: For all-cause mortality, MRAs reduced risk by 22% (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.72–0.85; P < 0.00001) with moderate heterogeneity ( I ² = 43%) ( Figure 4D )

quotes.quote: This study included a total of nine RCTs

scope.reading: Zhang 2025 pools nine MRA trials across HFrEF, HFmrEF/HFpEF and diabetic kidney disease; its 9 is not our target. The analysis that answers our question is Figure 4D (HFrEF all-cause mortality): RALES, EPHESUS and EMPHASIS-HF. Two are ours (RALES, EMPHASIS-HF). EPHESUS enrolled acute post-myocardial-infarction LV dysfunction, which our preregistered population excludes (X2), so it is a scope difference, not a missed trial. Our third trial, J-EMPHASIS-HF, is not in it.
scope.reported_by: external review of the spironolactone-hfref-mortality topic (28 Sep 2026)

method_difference.heading: Different trials, different model

quotes.quote: For all-cause mortality, MRAs reduced risk by 22% (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.72–0.85; P < 0.00001) with moderate heterogeneity ( I ² = 43%) ( Figure 4D )

method_difference.reading: Its 0.78 (0.72-0.85) is a fixed-effect pool of two of our trials plus EPHESUS (48.4% of its weight), outside our population; our 0.73 (0.56-0.95) is Paule-Mandel with a Hartung-Knapp interval over RALES, EMPHASIS-HF and J-EMPHASIS-HF. Agreement or disagreement between the two is not a check on either.
method_difference.reported_by: external review of the spironolactone-hfref-mortality topic (28 Sep 2026)
